l.entradas.astronomia-babilonica.lectura: In 2016, Mathieu Ossendrijver showed in the journal Science that some Babylonian astronomers calculated the displacement of Jupiter as the area of a trapezoid on a graph of velocity against time. It is an abstract procedure that anticipates ideas of integral calculus. Jupiter was Marduk's star. The finding shows Babylonian astronomy as a mathematical science, far removed from fantasies about "hidden planets" such as Nibiru.
l.entradas.nibiru.titulo_actual: From astronomical point to apocalyptic myth
l.entradas.nibiru.lectura: In the cuneiform texts, Nibiru is an astronomical "crossing point" linked to Marduk, identified above all with Jupiter. Current reception studies are interested in how Zecharia Sitchin turned it into a wandering planet and how, in the 21st century, it gave rise to apocalyptic prophecies that spread over the internet (2003, 2012, 2017). It is a textbook case of how a modern myth is created and circulates, and astronomers reject it.
l.entradas.anunnaki.lectura: For Assyriology, the Anunnaki are a collective of gods whose role changes with the period. Today their main public life is in popular culture, which draws on Sitchin and on series such as Ancient Aliens. Cultural studies analyze this phenomenon as an appropriation that strips the Sumerians of the authorship of their own civilization, and some critics relate that reasoning to colonial prejudices.
l.entradas.lamassu.lectura: The winged bulls of the Assyrian palaces are today a symbol of heritage in danger. In 2015 the Islamic State released videos in which it destroyed lamassu at Nineveh and Nimrud. The Iraqi-American artist Michael Rakowitz responded with a replica made of date syrup cans, installed on the Fourth Plinth in Trafalgar Square (London, 2018). Postcolonial criticism also asks why the most famous lamassu are in London, Paris or Chicago and not in Iraq.
l.entradas.kur-inframundo.lectura: The Mesopotamian Underworld, dark and the same for everyone, where the dead eat dust, appears in studies of death as a radically unconsoling vision. That is why it is compared with the Greek Hades and the biblical Sheol. The discovery of Ni 12501, with a storm god trapped in the Underworld, broadens the repertoire of descents beyond that of Inanna.
l.entradas.zigurat.lectura: The ziggurats, especially the one at Ur, partially restored under Saddam Hussein, are examples of how modern Iraq has used the Mesopotamian past to build a national identity. Postcolonial studies analyze these political uses and the military damage to sites such as Ur or Babylon during the wars of 1991 and 2003.
l.entradas.apkallu-oannes.lectura: The apkallu, half-man, half-fish sages who taught the arts to humanity, are studied today as a figure of scribal ideology: written knowledge would have a divine origin and an unbroken transmission down to the scholars of each age. Their frequent use in ancient astronaut literature is itself an object of study for those who analyze reception.
l.hallazgos.2003-0.descripcion: In April 2003, after the fall of Baghdad, the National Museum of Iraq was looted. At first there was talk of 170,000 objects; later the figures dropped to several thousand, and Zainab Bahrani estimated more than 20,000. The investigation led by Colonel Matthew Bogdanos recovered part of them, and the episode became a central case in debates on heritage and war.
l.hallazgos.2014-0.descripcion: Irving Finkel, of the British Museum, published The Ark Before Noah. In the book he studies an Old Babylonian tablet in which the flood hero, Atrahasis, receives instructions to build a round ark, a kind of giant coracle. The finding aroused great media interest in the relationship between this story and that of Noah.
l.hallazgos.2014-1.descripcion: The Sulaymaniyah Museum (Iraqi Kurdistan) bought a tablet, T.1447, in 2011, in which Farouk Al-Rawi and Andrew George identified some 20 new lines of Tablet V. They published it in the Journal of Cuneiform Studies 66 (2014), and the news spread in 2015. The Cedar Forest appears full of birds, cicadas and monkeys, and Enkidu seems to regret its destruction.
l.hallazgos.2015-0.descripcion: The Islamic State released videos in which it destroyed Assyrian reliefs and lamassu in the Mosul Museum, at Nineveh and at Nimrud. These events spurred digital documentation and reconstruction projects, and made Mesopotamian heritage a subject of worldwide debate.
l.hallazgos.2016-0.descripcion: Mathieu Ossendrijver published in Science (vol. 351) that four tablets in the British Museum calculate the displacement of Jupiter as the area under a graph of velocity against time. They are the first evidence of geometric methods in Babylonian mathematical astronomy, which until then had been considered purely arithmetical.
l.hallazgos.2021-0.titulo: Return of the Gilgamesh Dream Tablet
l.hallazgos.2021-0.descripcion: The tablet had been looted in Iraq, was sold with a false provenance and was bought by Hobby Lobby in 2014 for 1.67 million dollars for the Museum of the Bible. It was seized in 2019, forfeited in July 2021 and handed over to Iraq at a ceremony held in Washington in September 2021. It is a symbol of the fight against antiquities trafficking.
l.hallazgos.2023-0.titulo: The Electronic Babylonian Library Fragmentarium opens
l.hallazgos.2023-0.descripcion: On February 3, 2023, Enrique Jiménez's team (LMU Munich) opened the eBL database to the public. It contains thousands of photographed and transliterated fragments and an automatic tool for finding joins between them.
l.hallazgos.2023-1.titulo: Machine translation of Akkadian (Gutherz et al.)
l.hallazgos.2023-1.descripcion: Gai Gutherz, Shai Gordin, Luis Sáenz, Omer Levy and Jonathan Berant presented in PNAS Nexus a neural model that translates Akkadian into English, both from the cuneiform signs and from transliteration. It reaches BLEU4 scores of about 37 and works best with short sentences. The authors present it as an aid for specialists, not as a substitute.
l.hallazgos.2024-0.titulo: Gilgamesh fragments joined with the help of AI
l.hallazgos.2024-0.descripcion: According to press reports in 2024, the eBL team had joined more than 1,500 fragments. Among them are some 20 from Gilgamesh, which complete or improve more than 100 lines, and pieces of an unknown hymn to the city of Babylon. Some of these findings already appear in the translations by Andrew George (2020) and Sophus Helle (2021).
l.hallazgos.2024-1.titulo: The myth of Enlil and Iškur (Ni 12501)
l.hallazgos.2024-1.descripcion: Jana Matuszak published in Iraq 86 (2024) the first complete edition of Ni 12501. It is a Sumerian tablet from around 2400 BC in which Enlil looks for someone to rescue his son Iškur from the Underworld, and only the fox volunteers. The news reached the general press in July 2025.
l.hallazgos.2024-2.titulo: The Babylonian Map of the World and the "ark"
l.hallazgos.2024-2.descripcion: Irving Finkel publicly reinterpreted the Babylonian Map of the World (British Museum, found at Sippar in 1882). He linked it with the route to Urartu (Ararat) and with a term for the flood boat that appears only on one other tablet. It is Finkel's personal reading and is not shared by all specialists.
l.recepcion.gilgamesh-a-new-english-vers: It is a very free poetic version, made from other translations because the author does not read Akkadian. It offers an accessible Gilgamesh, more sexually explicit and with a Humbaba who arouses compassion. It was a bestseller and is criticized for being more an adaptation than a translation.
l.recepcion.gilgamesh-the-king-0.descrip: Historical novel narrated in the first person by Gilgamesh. It treats the gods as the characters' beliefs rather than as real beings, and develops the grief for Enkidu.
l.recepcion.gilgamesh-0.descripcion: Australian novel in which a young woman of the 1930s travels to Armenia. The epic serves as an echo of the quest, of loss and of the journey, not as a story retold.
l.recepcion.trilogia-de-gilgamesh-gilgam: Gilgamesh trilogy (Gilgamesh the King; The Revenge of Ishtar; The Last Quest of Gilgamesh)

Illustrated children's books, published between 1992 and 1995, with an aesthetic inspired by cylinder seals. They soften the violence and eroticism and highlight friendship and the acceptance of death.
l.recepcion.the-epic-of-gilgamesh-orator: Oratorio composed in 1954–1955 and premiered in Basel in 1958, with an English libretto based on Campbell Thompson's translation. It focuses on the death of Enkidu and the summoning of his spirit, an existential meditation on death.
l.recepcion.star-trek-the-next-generatio: Picard tells the story of Gilgamesh and Enkidu to the Tamarian captain Dathon as he dies. The myth becomes a metaphor for communication between cultures: two enemies who become friends in the face of a common danger.
l.recepcion.gilgamesh-manga-0.descripcio: Science fiction manga published between 1976 and 1978 that uses the name Gilgamesh for an apocalyptic story. The original version included extraterrestrials, who were removed in Group TAC's 2003 anime. That element points to the imagery of paleocontact, but there is no record that it comes from Sitchin.
l.recepcion.gilgamesh-ii-0.descripcion: Science fiction miniseries that transfers the archetype of the demigod king and his friendship with a "wild man" to a galactic future. Not verified in online sources.
l.recepcion.eternals-pelicula-0.descripc: Gilgamesh, played by Ma Dong-seok, is one of the Eternals, beings created by the cosmic Celestials who inspired human myths. Jack Kirby's concept (1976) draws on the paleocontact ideas of the 1970s, more on von Däniken than on Sitchin.
l.recepcion.final-fantasy-v-y-saga-0.des: Gilgamesh is a wandering, comic swordsman and weapons collector, accompanied by Enkidu, and his fight on the Big Bridge is famous. Of the myth only the names and the idea of an endless quest remain. He reappears in many later installments.
l.recepcion.fate-stay-night-0.descripcio: Gilgamesh, the "King of Heroes", is an arrogant servant who owns all the treasures of the world. He represents the tyrant before the friendship with Enkidu, who in the series appears as an androgynous being.
l.recepcion.fate-grand-order-absolute-de: Fate/Grand Order – Absolute Demonic Front: Babylonia (anime)
Series of 21 episodes (2019–2020) set in a mythical Uruk, with a wiser Gilgamesh who is already an administrator king, as well as Ishtar, Ereshkigal and a monstrous Tiamat as primordial mother.
l.recepcion.smite-panteon-babilonio-0.de: A combat game between gods. Its "Babylonian" pantheon includes Tiamat, Gilgamesh (added in April 2021, who faces Tiamat) and Ishtar (August 2022, goddess of love and war with a bow). It mixes Sumerian and Babylonian figures without distinguishing periods.
l.recepcion.civilization-vi-0.descripcio: Gilgamesh leads Sumeria, and his ability "Adventures with Enkidu" turns the friendship of the epic into military alliances. It is an image of the historical-legendary king as strategist and builder.
l.recepcion.stargate-sg-1-the-tomb-0.des: In the series, the ancient gods are parasitic aliens (the Goa'uld). In this episode the team finds the tomb of Marduk in a ziggurat. It is a clear example of the ancient astronaut scheme; the Stargate franchise has been linked with Sitchin's ideas. Episode details not verified.
l.recepcion.ancient-aliens-0.descripcion: A pseudoscientific popular documentary series that repeats Sitchin's theses: the Anunnaki as astronauts from Nibiru who created humanity through genetic engineering. It is the main channel through which these ideas reach the public today.
l.recepcion.prometheus-0.descripcion: Alien "Engineers" would have created humanity and left star maps in ancient cultures, including the Mesopotamian one. It takes up the scheme of creator gods from space spread by Sitchin and others.
l.recepcion.the-conduit-0.descripcion: A shooter about alien conspiracies. According to Skeptoid, it took part of its concept from Sitchin's ideas.
l.recepcion.the-invisible-enemy-should-n: The Invisible Enemy Should Not Exist (Lamassu)

Sculpture installed on the Fourth Plinth in Trafalgar Square: a lamassu from Nineveh destroyed in 2015, rebuilt with some 10,500 cans of Iraqi date syrup. It is a postcolonial reinterpretation that speaks of destruction, diaspora and heritage.
